examples.en: I put a hook on the wall and hung my bag on it.
The captain is a pirate with a hook for one hand.
The string is caught on the hook and won't come loose.
At the butcher's, meat is hanging from hooks.

examples.ko: 갈고리 모양 손잡이가 달린 지팡이를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a cane with a hook-shaped handle.
The cat's claws are sharp like hooks.

explain: '걸이'나 '고리'는 걸어 두는 물건 전체에 쓰고, '갈고리'는 끝이 굽은 모양을 강조해요. 그래서 물건을 낚거나 매달 때 쓰는 날카로운 쇠붙이에 어울려요. '손'이나 '발톱' 모양을 말할 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: 걸이 and 고리 are general words for things that hold other things, while 갈고리 stresses a bent, pointed end. It suits a sharp metal piece used to catch or hang things. It is also often used to describe the shape of hands or claws.

examples.en: I bought a drill to make a hole in the wall.

examples.ko: 드릴 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The drill noise was so loud that I was startled.
The neighbors are working with a drill.

examples.ko: 전동 드릴은 나사를 박을 때도 편해요.
examples.en: An electric drill is also handy for driving in screws.
My father showed me how to use a drill.

examples.ko: 드릴을 쓸 때는 보안경을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear safety glasses when using a drill.

explain: 벽이나 나무에 구멍을 뚫는 공구예요. 전기로 돌리는 것은 '전동 드릴'이라고 해요. 영어 drill에는 '반복 훈련'이라는 뜻도 있지만 한국어 드릴은 보통 공구를 가리켜요.
explain_en: This is the tool for boring holes in walls or wood; the electric kind is called 전동 드릴. English drill also means repeated practice, but in Korean 드릴 usually points to the tool.

examples.en: Please close the bottle cap tightly.
When I pulled the bathtub plug, the water drained.
The cap wouldn't open, so I popped it with a spoon.

examples.ko: 샴푸 마개를 열고 한 번 눌렀어요.
examples.en: I opened the shampoo cap and pressed once.
I sealed the bottle with a cork stopper.
There was no stopper, so all the water spilled.

explain: '뚜껑'은 위에서 덮는 것이고, '마개'는 구멍에 끼워 막는 것이에요. 그래서 '병마개'라고 하지만 냄비에는 '냄비 뚜껑'이라고 해요. '마개를 따다/열다/막다'로 써요.
explain_en: A '뚜껑' covers from the top, while a '마개' is pushed into an opening to block it. So it is '병마개', but for a pot it is '냄비 뚜껑'. You say '마개를 따다/열다/막다'.

examples.ko: 불씨가 꺼지지 않게 장작을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: I added more firewood so the embers would not die out.

examples.ko: 작은 불씨 하나가 큰 산불로 번졌어요.
examples.en: One small ember spread into a big forest fire.

examples.ko: 모닥불의 불씨를 물로 꼭 꺼야 해요.
examples.en: You must put out the embers of the campfire with water.
Grandmother left embers in the fireplace.
Without a lighter it was hard to get a spark going.

examples.ko: 불씨가 아직 살아 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The embers are still alive, so we have to be careful.

explain: 불씨는 꺼지지 않고 남아 있는 작은 불이에요. 튀어 오르는 작은 불덩이는 '불똥'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 비유로 큰 문제를 일으킬 작은 원인에도 써요.

phrases.example: 작은 오해가 큰 싸움의 불씨가 됐어요.
phrases.en: A small misunderstanding became the spark of a big fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 갈등이나 사건이 시작되는 작은 원인을 말할 때 비유로 써요. 싸움, 논란, 갈등과 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for the small cause that starts a big conflict or incident. It often appears with fights, controversies and conflicts.

explain_en: 불씨 is a small fire that stays alive and can start a bigger one. '불똥' is different: it is a small flying spark. Figuratively, 불씨 is a small cause that can grow into a big problem.

examples.en: The children draw pictures on the ground with a stick.
Grandfather walks leaning on a stick.
I picked fruit using just one stick.

examples.ko: 텐트를 작대기 몇 개로 받쳐 놓았어요.
examples.en: I propped up the tent with a few poles.
The stick I picked up on the road is quite sturdy.
I tied a string to a stick and made a fishing rod.

explain: '막대기'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 군대에서는 계급장의 줄을 '작대기'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '막대기'. In the military, the stripes on a rank insignia are also called '작대기'.

examples.en: I stocked up on a lot of ramen during the sale.

examples.ko: 태풍이 온다고 해서 물을 쟁여 놨어요.
examples.en: A typhoon was coming, so I stored up water.
I have a habit of stocking the fridge with side dishes.
Grandmother keeps rice stored up in the shed.

examples.ko: 책을 방에 쟁이면 걸어 다니기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you pile books up in the room, it's hard to walk around.

examples.ko: 좋아하는 과자를 쟁일 수 있어서 기뻐요.
examples.en: I'm happy I can stock up on my favorite snacks.

explain: '쌓다'는 위로 높이 올리는 것이고, '쟁이다'는 나중에 쓰려고 많이 모아 두는 것이에요. 말할 때는 '쟁여 두다', '쟁여 놓다'로 많이 쓰고, 할인할 때 사 두는 것을 '쟁이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '쌓다' is stacking things up high; '쟁이다' is stockpiling a lot for later use. In speech it's usually '쟁여 두다' or '쟁여 놓다', and also for buying extra on sale.
